body:
A good contractor invoice has 10 parts: your business details, the client, a unique invoice number, dates, itemized work with quantities and rates, materials, tax, deposit paid, balance due, and payment terms. Miss one and payment slows down. Use the copy-ready template below on your next job and you will spend less time chasing money.

## What must a contractor invoice include?

Think of the invoice as the paper trail for the whole job. It has to stand on its own months later, for the customer, for your books, and for tax time.

1. **Your business name, address, phone, and email.** Use the legal name that matches your Form W-9, not a short nickname.
2. **Client name and job address.** The billing address and the work address are often different. Show both.
3. **Unique invoice number.** Number in order, INV-1041, INV-1042, and never reuse one. Gaps and repeats look sloppy and cause mix ups in accounting software.
4. **Invoice date and work dates.** The invoice date starts the payment clock. Work dates prove when the job was done.
5. **Itemized lines.** Each line gets a plain description, a quantity, a unit rate, and a line total. Labor by the hour, materials by the item, flat work by the job.
6. **Subtotal, tax, and total.** Show tax on its own line with the rate you used. Tax rules on labor and materials vary by state, so check yours.
7. **Deposit paid and balance due.** List payments already made, then the balance in bold. This is the number the customer acts on.
8. **Payment terms and due date.** Net 14 or Net 30, plus the exact date. Add how you take payment and any late fee you charge, stated the same way your contract states it.
9. **License number where your state requires it.** Some states require it on contracts and invoices for construction work.
10. **A short thank you and a contact for questions.** One line is enough. It gets invoices paid faster than a stern note does.

On the tax side, clients who pay you for services may need your taxpayer information to file Form 1099-NEC at year end. They get that from your Form W-9, which the IRS says a payer should ask for before work begins. Keep your full tax ID on the W-9 in the client file. Do not print a full Social Security number on an invoice that gets emailed and forwarded.

Start from a clean quote and the invoice almost writes itself. Our [free estimate template](/blog/free-estimate-template/) uses the same line layout, so the final bill matches the price the customer agreed to.

## Copy-ready invoice template you can use today

Copy this block into a document or spreadsheet and replace the bracketed parts. Keep the order. It matches the worked example below.

```
INVOICE
[Your Business Name]                    Invoice No: [INV-1042]
[Street Address]                        Invoice Date: [Oct 20, 2026]
[City, State ZIP]                       Work Dates: [Oct 12 to Oct 16, 2026]
[Phone] | [Email]                       Due Date: [Nov 3, 2026]
[License No, if required]

Bill To:
[Client Name]
[Job Address]
[Billing Address, if different]

Description                  Qty    Rate      Amount
------------------------------------------------------
[Labor - describe the work]  [16]   [$65.00]  [$1,040.00]
[Material - paint, gallons]  [ ]    [ ]       [ ]
[Material - primer]          [ ]    [ ]       [ ]
[Supplies]                   [ ]    [ ]       [ ]
------------------------------------------------------
Subtotal                                [ ]
Tax ([rate] percent on [materials])     [ ]
Total                                   [ ]
Deposit Paid                            [ ]
BALANCE DUE                             [ ]

Terms: Due in [14] days. Pay by [check, card, or transfer to details on file].
Late payments: [1.5 percent per month, as stated in your contract].
Questions: [Name, phone].
Thank you for your business.
```

Prefer to fill it in on screen? The invoice builder at the top of this page does the same math, including tax on materials only and the deposit, and prints a clean copy or saves it as a PDF. Save a blank copy as your master. For each job, save a new copy with the invoice number in the file name. That habit alone ends most lost invoice problems.

## Worked example: a living room repaint invoice

Here is the same template filled in for a real size job. Paint a living room, walls and ceiling, two coats.

Labor line: 16 hours x $65.00 per hour = $1,040.00.

Materials lines: paint $185.00, primer $65.00, supplies (tape, rollers, drop cloths) $40.00. Materials total: $185 + $65 + $40 = $290.00.

Subtotal: $1,040.00 + $290.00 = $1,330.00.

Tax: this example charges 7 percent tax on materials only. $290.00 x 0.07 = $20.30.

Total: $1,330.00 + $20.30 = $1,350.30.

Deposit paid: the customer paid $400.00 at signing.

Balance due: $1,350.30 - $400.00 = $950.30.

Check the math a second way. Add the balance and the deposit: $950.30 + $400.00 = $1,350.30, which is the total. Then check the total build up: labor $1,040.00 + materials $290.00 + tax $20.30 = $1,350.30. Both checks match.

Terms on this invoice: due in 14 days, by Nov 3, 2026. The rate behind the labor line came from working out a full charge out rate first. If yours is a guess, fix it with our [contractor hourly rate calculator](/blog/contractor-hourly-rate-calculator/) before the next quote.

## How do you number, send, and track invoices?

Number in one unbroken run for the whole business. Do not restart at 1 for each customer. One run makes year end work simple and proves no invoice is missing.

Send the invoice the day the work is done, while the job still looks great in the customer mind. Attach photos of the finished work if the job is hard to see, like work in an attic or under a deck. Send a PDF, not a file the customer has to edit to read.

Track three dates for each invoice: sent, due, and paid. A simple list on one page beats a memory. Review it every Friday. An invoice that is 7 days late gets a polite note. At 14 days, a phone call. At 30 days, a formal letter that points back to the signed contract and the late terms printed on the invoice.

Keep copies for at least four years. The IRS guidance on information returns notes that payers keep Form W-9 on file for four years for reference, and your own invoices deserve the same care. They are your proof of income and your best defense in a dispute.

## Mistakes that delay payment

The top mistake is a lump sum with no lines. A single line that says labor and materials, $1,350.30, gives the customer nothing to check and gives an accounts clerk nothing to approve. Itemize and it moves.

Next is a missing due date. Net 30 written with no date makes the customer do math. Print the date.

Third is a balance that hides the deposit. If the customer paid $400 and your invoice shows only the full total, expect a confused call and a slow check. Show deposit paid and balance due every time.

Fourth is terms that differ from the contract. If the contract says 1.5 percent per month late and the invoice says 2 percent, you have a fight you created. Copy the words across word for word. If you also price change orders, show each approved change as its own line with the date it was approved. That one habit ends most end of job arguments. Our guide on [markup vs margin](/blog/markup-vs-margin-calculator/) helps you price those changes right in the first place.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the difference between an estimate, an invoice, and a receipt?
An estimate or quote is the price before work, an invoice is the bill after work, and a receipt is proof of payment. Use the same line layout for the estimate and the invoice so the customer can compare them line by line.

### Do I need to charge sales tax on a contractor invoice?
It depends on your state and on the kind of work. Many states tax materials but not labor for real property work, and rules differ for repairs versus improvements. Show the tax you charge on its own line, and confirm your rule with your state tax office or accountant before your first invoice.

### How long should I give a customer to pay?
Net 14 is common for small residential jobs, Net 30 for commercial work. Shorter terms keep cash moving. Whatever you pick, print the exact due date on the invoice and match it to the contract the customer signed.

### Should my tax ID go on the invoice?
Put your business name exactly as it appears on your Form W-9, and give the client a completed W-9 for their file. Avoid printing a full Social Security number on invoices. If you have an EIN, that is the safer number to share for business paperwork.

### What do I do if a customer disputes a line?
Send the backup: the signed estimate, change order approvals, time records, and material receipts for that line. Most disputes are memory problems, not bad faith. A clear paper trail settles them in one email.

### Can I charge a late fee?
Yes, if your contract states it and your state allows it. Print the same late terms on the invoice. A common term is 1.5 percent per month on the overdue balance, but your contract and state law control what you can use.
